graph_diagnosis.summary: Inflation data, expected policy restraint, technology-growth appetite, and risk sentiment form a reusable equity-duration framework.
weaknesses: The technical-rebound narrative is a generic, historically contingent anchor rather than independent valuation evidence.
Most inflation, policy, and sentiment source events occur after the forecast cutoff and are provenance only, not forecast-time inputs.
The graph lacks independent technology earnings, valuation, breadth, and real-yield evidence.

search_factors.why_search: Inflation and real-rate expectations affect equity discount rates.
Expected policy restraint changes discount-rate pressure on growth equities.
Growth-equity performance requires earnings, guidance, valuation, and breadth confirmation.
Geopolitical and macro risk can alter equity risk premiums.

checkpoints.mechanism: Softer inflation can reduce expected discount-rate pressure on duration-sensitive equities.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Use only cutoff-available inflation, real-yield, and policy data; verify breadth and revisions.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Inflation persistence or rising real yields restores discount-rate pressure.

checkpoints.mechanism: Less restrictive expected policy can lower expected discount rates and support growth-equity risk appetite.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Verify cutoff-available policy futures, real yields, and Fed communications.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Markets reprice a more restrictive path.

checkpoints.mechanism: Technology buying is sustainable only when earnings revisions, guidance, valuation, and market breadth corroborate it.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Verify earnings revisions, guidance, valuations, and participation across technology constituents.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Rallies are narrow or earnings revisions deteriorate.

checkpoints.mechanism: Geopolitical or macro uncertainty can increase equity risk premiums and offset policy-driven optimism.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Verify volatility, credit spreads, geopolitical developments, and cross-asset risk pricing.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Risk metrics improve despite adverse headlines.

checkpoints.mechanism: Infer Nasdaq direction only after reconciling cutoff-compliant real yields, policy pricing, earnings revisions, valuations, breadth, and risk sentiment.
checkpoints.evidence_requirement: Verify cutoff-available real yields, rate futures, technology earnings and guidance, valuation, breadth, volatility, and credit spreads without using a realized index move.
checkpoints.contradiction_signal: Real yields, earnings breadth, or risk premiums conflict with the proposed mechanism.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: Softer inflation can reprice policy and reduce discount-rate pressure on growth equities.
applicability_conditions: The repricing is visible in cutoff-available real yields and rate markets.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: Earnings and valuation confirmation can support technology equity demand.
applicability_conditions: Revisions, guidance, and market breadth corroborate demand.
failure_conditions: Participation is narrow or fundamentals weaken.

causal_paths.generalized_mechanism: Higher risk premiums can offset lower discount-rate pressure.
applicability_conditions: Risk pricing confirms the adverse sentiment channel.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Policy expectations improve but earnings and valuation do not validate technology demand.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminating_evidence: Compare real yields with earnings revisions, valuation, and market breadth.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: Risk-premium expansion dominates the discount-rate channel.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminating_evidence: Compare volatility and credit spreads with real yields and policy futures.

forecast_audit_questions: Do real yields and policy futures confirm lower discount-rate pressure?
Do technology earnings, valuation, and breadth corroborate demand?
Do volatility and credit spreads offset the policy mechanism?
